name: RC / LC Filter Designer
blurb: component values from a cutoff frequency, with the magnitude response drawn
intro: Gives R and C (first-order RC) or L and C (second-order LC into a resistive load R) so the −3 dB point lands on the cutoff you ask for, then snaps them to standard values and draws the response those values really give. For LC the alignment sets Q; the −3 dB point is kept at the cutoff for every alignment.

inputs.label: Filter
options: LC low-pass (2nd order, series L, shunt C)
LC high-pass (2nd order, series C, shunt L)

inputs.label: R (RC) or load resistance (LC)
inputs.help: RC: the resistor you want. LC: the resistance the filter drives, which sets its damping.

inputs.label: Fix C instead (RC only)
inputs.help: Leave empty to fix R; write e.g. 100n to fix C and get R.

inputs.label: Resistor series
inputs.help: Capacitors and inductors are snapped to E12.

examples.title: Anti-aliasing RC low-pass at 1 kHz with 10 kΩ
LC low-pass at 10 MHz into 50 Ω, Butterworth

usage: Give topo (rc-lp, rc-hp, lc-lp, lc-hp), the −3 dB cutoff in Hz, R in ohms (the resistor for RC, the load for LC), optionally C in farads to fix instead of R (RC only), the LC alignment (butterworth, bessel, critical, cheby1) and the resistor series. It returns the exact and standard component values, the cutoff and Q the standard values give, attenuation and phase at multiples of the cutoff, and the magnitude response as chart data. Use it for anti-aliasing, decoupling, EMI and simple audio or RF filters.
sources: Second order into load R: H = 1/(1 − x² + j·x/Q), x = ω/ω0, ω0 = 1/√(LC), Q = R·√(C/L) (high-pass: −x² in the numerator) - e.g. Horowitz & Hill, The Art of Electronics, 3rd ed., ch. 1 and 6
Alignment Q values for 2nd order: Butterworth 0.7071, Bessel 0.5773, Chebyshev 1 dB 0.9565 - standard filter tables (e.g. Williams & Taylor, Electronic Filter Design Handbook)
